lessons.title: Right-sizing and cost optimisation for ML and AI
lessons.summary: Match instance types and endpoint options to load, scale with auto scaling, buy compute with the right purchasing option, track spend with Budgets and tags, and cut FM costs with caching, batch and the right throughput model.

sections.heading: Right-size before you buy
sections.body:
- **SageMaker Inference Recommender** load-tests a model on candidate instance types and reports latency, throughput and cost so you can pick the cheapest instance that meets your SLA.
- **CloudWatch utilisation metrics** reveal over-provisioning: a GPU endpoint at low GPUUtilization is a candidate for a smaller or CPU instance.
- **AWS Compute Optimizer** and **Trusted Advisor** give right-sizing and idle-resource recommendations for EC2-based infrastructure.
- Choose the **endpoint type** by traffic shape: spiky or intermittent traffic with small payloads suits **serverless**; large payloads or long processing suits **asynchronous** (it can scale to zero); offline scoring of a dataset suits **batch transform**, which leaves no idle endpoint.

sections.heading: Auto scaling
sections.body: Real-time endpoint variants scale with Application Auto Scaling. The common policy is **target tracking** on `SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance`; step and scheduled scaling are also available. Set a sensible **minimum** for steady traffic and use **cooldowns** to avoid thrashing. Load-test to find the invocations per instance a single instance can sustain before setting the target.

sections.heading: Purchasing options
sections.body:
| Option | Fits | Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| On-Demand | Unpredictable or short-lived work | Highest unit price |
| **Managed Spot Training** | Interruptible training jobs | Must **checkpoint** to S3 and set a max wait time; not for real-time endpoints |
| **Savings Plans** (including SageMaker Savings Plans) | Steady baseline usage over 1 or 3 years | Commitment to a spend per hour |
| Reserved / provisioned capacity | Guaranteed capacity for critical workloads | Commitment term |

Use **AWS Budgets** for alerts against a threshold, **Cost Explorer** to analyse trends, and **cost allocation tags** (for example `project`, `team`) on endpoints, training jobs and notebooks so costs can be attributed.

sections.heading: Foundation model cost levers
sections.body:
Generative AI costs are driven by **tokens**, plus embedding and vector-store costs for RAG (Skill 4.2.10).

- **Prompt caching** reuses a long, stable prompt prefix (system prompt, documents, tool definitions). Cache reads are cheaper than normal input tokens. Caching has a model-specific minimum prefix size and a short default TTL, and it is not supported with batch inference.
- **Batch inference** suits large, non-urgent jobs (files in and out of S3).
- **Provisioned Throughput** buys Model Units by the hour for predictable high volume. A **customised model** is served either through Provisioned Throughput or, for supported base models and Regions, through a **custom model deployment** that gives on-demand, pay-per-use inference.
- Pick a smaller model where quality allows, cap output tokens, and choose a vector store that matches query volume; for example, **S3 Vectors** is cost-effective for infrequent queries.

keyPoints: Inference Recommender benchmarks instance types for a model; utilisation metrics reveal over-provisioning.
Target tracking on SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance is the default endpoint scaling policy.
Managed Spot Training needs checkpointing; Spot is a training lever, not a real-time endpoint lever.
Savings Plans cover steady baseline usage; Budgets alert; Cost Explorer analyses; tags attribute.

FM cost levers: model choice, prompt caching, batch inference, output limits, Provisioned Throughput for steady volume; customised models need Provisioned Throughput or (for supported models) a custom model deployment.

gotchas.trap: Enabling Managed Spot Training without checkpoints for a multi-hour job.
gotchas.correct: Without checkpoints an interruption restarts training from scratch; write checkpoints to S3.

gotchas.trap: Buying a Savings Plan sized to peak traffic.
gotchas.correct: Commit to the steady baseline and cover peaks with On-Demand capacity and auto scaling.

gotchas.trap: Expecting prompt caching to reduce the cost of a Bedrock batch inference job.
gotchas.correct: Prompt caching is not supported with batch inference.

lessons.lab: Run an Inference Recommender default job on a registered model, compare the cost per inference of the top two instance types, then deploy the winner with a target tracking policy on SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance and tag the endpoint with a project cost allocation tag.

lessons.title: Securing ML workloads: identity, network and encryption
lessons.summary: Least-privilege execution roles, Bedrock API keys versus IAM credentials, private networking with VPCs and PrivateLink, network isolation, KMS encryption, secrets handling and vulnerability scanning in CI/CD.

sections.heading: Identity: roles, policies and API keys
sections.body:
- Every SageMaker AI job, endpoint and notebook runs as an **execution role**. Scope it to the specific S3 prefixes, ECR repositories and KMS keys it needs, not `*`.
- Use **condition keys** to enforce guardrails, for example requiring a VPC configuration or a KMS key on `CreateTrainingJob`.
- **Bedrock API keys**: **short-term** keys last up to 12 hours (or the session), inherit the IAM principal's permissions and are recommended for production. **Long-term** keys create an IAM user with a set expiry and are for exploration only. Control use with `bedrock:CallWithBearerToken` and the `bedrock:bearerTokenType` condition key, and cap long-term key age with `iam:ServiceSpecificCredentialAgeDays`. Calls are recorded in CloudTrail.
- Store database passwords and third-party API tokens in **Secrets Manager**, not in code or environment variables baked into images.

sections.heading: Network: VPCs, PrivateLink and isolation
sections.body:
- Attach training jobs, processing jobs and endpoints to **private subnets and security groups** in your VPC so they can reach private data sources.
- Use **interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)** for the SageMaker API and runtime and for Bedrock, plus an **S3 gateway endpoint**, so traffic stays on the AWS network without an internet gateway or NAT.
- **Network isolation** blocks the container from making any outbound network calls, which protects against exfiltration by untrusted code. SageMaker still moves the input data and model artifacts for you.
- For distributed training, enable **inter-container traffic encryption**.
- Note: serverless endpoints do not support VPC configuration or network isolation.

sections.heading: Encryption and data protection
sections.body:
- Use **AWS KMS customer managed keys** for training volumes, model artifacts in S3, endpoint storage and Feature Store. Key policies plus IAM decide who can decrypt, and every use of the key is logged.
- Encrypt data in transit with TLS; SageMaker and Bedrock API endpoints are HTTPS.
- **Amazon Macie** discovers sensitive data (PII) in S3 buckets that feed training or RAG.
- **Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filters** block or mask PII in prompts and responses at inference time.

sections.heading: Securing the pipeline
sections.body: Skill 4.3.1 names **Amazon Inspector** (vulnerability scanning of ECR container images, Lambda functions and EC2) and **Amazon CodeGuru** (code review findings) as CI/CD controls. Add them as gates in CodePipeline so a model container with critical CVEs never reaches an endpoint. Track configuration drift with **AWS Config** and API activity with **CloudTrail**.

keyPoints: Least-privilege execution roles scoped to specific buckets, repositories and keys.
Short-term Bedrock API keys for production; long-term keys only for exploration.
PrivateLink interface endpoints keep SageMaker and Bedrock traffic off the internet; add an S3 gateway endpoint.
Network isolation blocks all outbound calls from the container.
KMS customer managed keys give control and audit of who can decrypt ML data and artifacts.
Inspector scans container images; CodeGuru reviews code; both fit as CI/CD gates.

gotchas.trap: Adding a NAT gateway so a private endpoint can call the SageMaker runtime API.
gotchas.correct: Use an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for the SageMaker runtime; no internet path is needed.

gotchas.trap: Handing a long-term Bedrock API key to a production service.
gotchas.correct: Long-term keys are for exploration; production should use IAM roles or short-term keys.

gotchas.trap: Expecting a serverless endpoint to run inside your VPC.
gotchas.correct: Serverless Inference does not support VPC configuration; use a real-time endpoint for private networking.

lessons.lab: Create a VPC with private subnets, add interface endpoints for sagemaker.api and sagemaker.runtime plus an S3 gateway endpoint, then deploy a real-time endpoint with a VPC config, network isolation and a KMS customer managed key. Invoke it from a Lambda function in the same VPC.

lessons.title: Guardrails, governance and audit
lessons.summary: Apply Bedrock Guardrails to model inputs and outputs, document models with Model Cards and Model Registry, trace artifacts with lineage, and audit with CloudTrail and AWS Config.

sections.heading: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sections.body:
Guardrails apply configurable safeguards to **both prompts and responses**:

- **Content filters** — Hate, Insults, Sexual, Violence, Misconduct and **Prompt Attack** (jailbreak and injection) for text and images, with adjustable strength.
- **Denied topics** — topics the application must refuse, defined in natural language.
- **Word filters** — exact words and phrases, including profanity.
- **Sensitive information filters** — block or **mask** PII types, plus custom regex.
- **Contextual grounding checks** — score whether a response is grounded in the retrieved source and relevant to the query, catching RAG hallucinations.
- **Automated Reasoning checks** — validate responses against formal rules.

Guardrails can run **inline** with model invocation or **standalone with the `ApplyGuardrail` API**, which lets you screen text for any model, including ones hosted outside Bedrock. They are versioned, so production can pin a tested version.

sections.heading: Model governance: Model Cards, Model Registry and lineage
sections.body:
- **SageMaker Model Cards** document intended use, risk rating, training details and evaluation results in one place, and can be exported for auditors.
- **Model Registry** organises versions in model package groups with an **approval status** (for example PendingManualApproval to Approved) that can gate CI/CD deployment, and it shows Model Cards and lineage.
- **Lineage tracking** links datasets, processing and training jobs, models and endpoints so you can answer "which data trained the model behind this endpoint?"
- **MLflow on SageMaker AI** tracks experiments and can auto-register models into Model Registry.

sections.heading: Audit and compliance
sections.body:
- **AWS CloudTrail** records who called which SageMaker AI or Bedrock API, when and from where.
- **AWS Config** records resource configuration over time and evaluates rules, for example flagging endpoints without a KMS key or notebooks with direct internet access.
- Combine these with invocation logging for content-level audit, and with Model Cards for documentation-level audit.

keyPoints: Guardrails filter both inputs and outputs: content, denied topics, words, PII, contextual grounding, Automated Reasoning.
ApplyGuardrail screens text independently of model invocation, including for non-Bedrock models.
Model Cards document; Model Registry versions and approves; lineage traces data to endpoint.
CloudTrail answers "who did what"; AWS Config answers "how is it configured and is it compliant".

gotchas.trap: Using a denied topic to stop RAG answers that are not supported by retrieved documents.
gotchas.correct: Use contextual grounding checks, which score grounding and relevance against the source.

gotchas.trap: Relying on Model Cards to block deployment of unapproved models.
gotchas.correct: Model Cards document; gating is done with Model Registry approval status in the CI/CD pipeline.

flashcards.front: Which data formats does the MLA-C02 guide name for storage choices based on access patterns?
flashcards.back: Parquet, JSON, CSV and ORC.

flashcards.front: Why do Parquet and ORC make Athena queries cheaper?
flashcards.back: They are columnar and compressed, so queries read only the columns (and partitions) they need instead of whole rows.

flashcards.front: What is RecordIO-protobuf?
flashcards.back: A binary record format accepted by many SageMaker built-in algorithms. Background knowledge only; the C02 guide names Parquet, JSON, CSV and ORC.

flashcards.front: Kinesis Data Streams vs Data Firehose?
flashcards.back: Data Streams: durable shards with consumers you write, multiple readers. Firehose: fully managed buffered delivery to destinations such as S3, with optional format conversion.

flashcards.front: How can a stream land in S3 as Parquet with no custom code?
flashcards.back: Data Firehose record format conversion (JSON to Parquet or ORC) using a Glue table schema.

flashcards.front: When is Managed Service for Apache Flink the right choice?
flashcards.back: Stateful, low-latency stream processing such as windowed aggregations or joins for near-real-time features.

flashcards.front: AWS Glue vs Amazon EMR for Spark ETL?
flashcards.back: Glue: serverless, integrated with the Data Catalog and crawlers. EMR: managed clusters with control over software, libraries and configuration.

flashcards.front: Which vector stores support binary vectors for Bedrock Knowledge Bases?
flashcards.back: Only Amazon OpenSearch Serverless and OpenSearch Service managed clusters.

flashcards.front: When does Amazon S3 Vectors fit a Knowledge Base?
flashcards.back: Cost-sensitive, infrequently queried workloads; sub-second queries, float embeddings only, limited metadata per vector.

flashcards.front: Can a Knowledge Base use an OpenSearch managed domain that is only reachable in a VPC?
flashcards.back: No. Managed domains behind a VPC are not supported for Knowledge Bases; public access is required.

flashcards.front: What must match between an embedding model and a vector index?
flashcards.back: The vector dimension. Changing the model or dimension means re-embedding the corpus into a new index.

flashcards.front: What is the default Knowledge Base chunking?
flashcards.back: About 300 tokens per chunk, honouring sentence boundaries.

flashcards.front: How does hierarchical chunking work?
flashcards.back: Small child chunks are matched for precision, then the larger parent chunk is returned for context. Not recommended with S3 Vectors.

flashcards.front: Why does semantic chunking cost extra?
flashcards.back: It uses a foundation model to find meaning-based breakpoints.

flashcards.front: When do you choose "no chunking" in a Knowledge Base?
flashcards.back: When documents are already split as you want, or you do custom chunking in a Lambda transformation.

flashcards.front: Where does SageMaker Data Wrangler live now?
flashcards.back: It is integrated into SageMaker Canvas, with a natural-language interface.

flashcards.front: Where can a Data Wrangler flow be exported?
flashcards.back: Amazon S3, SageMaker Pipelines, SageMaker Feature Store, or a Python script.

flashcards.front: What does the Data Wrangler Data Quality and Insights report detect?
flashcards.back: Data anomalies and issues including target leakage.

flashcards.front: What is AWS Glue DataBrew for?
flashcards.back: Visual, no-code data profiling and cleaning with reusable recipes, aimed at analysts.

flashcards.front: Mean vs median imputation?
flashcards.back: Mean suits roughly symmetric data; median is robust to outliers and skew.

flashcards.front: One-hot vs ordinal encoding?
flashcards.back: One-hot for nominal categories (no order). Ordinal only when categories have a real order.

flashcards.front: Which models need feature scaling most?
flashcards.back: Distance- and gradient-based models (k-NN, linear models, neural networks). Tree-based models are largely insensitive.

flashcards.front: How do you avoid leakage when scaling or imputing?
flashcards.back: Split first, fit the transform on the training split only, then apply it to validation and test data.

flashcards.front: Feature Store online vs offline store?
flashcards.back: Online: latest record per ID, low-latency reads for inference. Offline: append-only history in S3 Parquet, queried with Athena for training.

flashcards.front: Which two features does every Feature Store feature group need?
flashcards.back: A record identifier and an event time.

flashcards.front: How do you ingest a single streaming record into Feature Store?
flashcards.back: The synchronous PutRecord API.

flashcards.front: What problem does a shared feature store reduce?
flashcards.back: Training-serving skew, because training and inference use the same feature definitions and pipeline.

flashcards.front: Class Imbalance (CI) vs Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL)?
flashcards.back: CI: one group has far fewer members. DPL: positive-label rates differ between groups.

flashcards.front: What is the status of SageMaker Clarify, Ground Truth and Model Monitor in late 2026?
flashcards.back: In maintenance and closed to new customers. Ground Truth Plus reached end of support on 30 Jun 2026.

flashcards.front: Which tools does the C02 guide name for data quality validation?
flashcards.back: AWS Glue DataBrew and AWS Glue Data Quality.

flashcards.front: Macie vs Comprehend vs Guardrails for PII?
flashcards.back: Macie finds PII in S3. Comprehend detects and redacts PII in text. Guardrails sensitive information filters block or mask PII in prompts and responses.

flashcards.front: What format does Bedrock fine-tuning data use?
flashcards.back: JSONL: {"prompt","completion"} records, or conversational records with schemaVersion "bedrock-conversation-2024".

flashcards.front: What do you supply for Bedrock model distillation?
flashcards.back: Prompts. A teacher model generates the responses used to fine-tune the student model.

flashcards.front: How should a time-series dataset be split?
flashcards.back: Chronologically, so validation and test data come after the training period.

flashcards.front: Which AWS AI service extracts text, key-value pairs and tables from scanned documents?
flashcards.back: Amazon Textract.

flashcards.front: Which AWS AI service detects sentiment, entities and PII in text?
flashcards.back: Amazon Comprehend.

flashcards.front: Which AWS AI service converts speech in audio files to text?
flashcards.back: Amazon Transcribe.

flashcards.front: SageMaker JumpStart vs Amazon Bedrock: who manages the inference instances?
flashcards.back: JumpStart deploys models to SageMaker AI endpoints in your account, where you choose and manage instances. Bedrock is serverless API access to FMs.

flashcards.front: When do you choose RAG over fine-tuning?
flashcards.back: When answers must use private or frequently changing knowledge, or need citations. Updating the knowledge base updates answers without retraining.

flashcards.front: What does Bedrock Custom Model Import do?
flashcards.back: Imports weights for supported open-weight architectures (Hugging Face format, from S3) so you can invoke them on demand through the Bedrock API.

flashcards.front: What is SageMaker AI script mode?
flashcards.back: Running your own training script in a prebuilt framework container (for example PyTorch or scikit-learn), passing hyperparameters as arguments, with minimal code changes.

flashcards.front: Data parallelism vs model parallelism?
flashcards.back: Data parallel: the model fits on one device, and data shards are split across devices. Model parallel: the model is too big for one device, so the model itself is split.

flashcards.front: What does SageMaker HyperPod add for FM training?
flashcards.back: Resilient clusters that automatically detect and replace faulty nodes, orchestrated by Slurm or Amazon EKS.

flashcards.front: What must you do to use Managed Spot Training safely?
flashcards.back: Write checkpoints to S3 so an interrupted job can resume, and set a maximum wait time.

flashcards.front: Signs of overfitting and two fixes?
flashcards.back: Low training error but high validation error. Fixes: L1/L2 regularisation or dropout, early stopping, more data, a simpler model.

flashcards.front: Signs of underfitting and a fix?
flashcards.back: High error on both training and validation data. Fix: more model capacity or better features, less regularisation.

flashcards.front: Bagging vs boosting?
flashcards.back: Bagging trains models in parallel on bootstrap samples and mainly reduces variance. Boosting trains models sequentially to correct earlier errors and mainly reduces bias.

flashcards.front: AMT grid search: what parameter types does it support?
flashcards.back: Categorical parameters only. AMT computes the number of training jobs automatically.

flashcards.front: Which AMT strategy is best for maximum concurrency?
flashcards.back: Random search, because each job is independent of earlier results.

flashcards.front: How does AMT Bayesian optimisation choose values?
flashcards.back: It treats tuning as a regression problem and uses previous results to balance exploration and exploitation, usually needing fewer jobs.

flashcards.front: Hyperband: what must TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType be set to?
flashcards.back: OFF. Hyperband has its own internal early stopping.

flashcards.front: Name the three Bedrock customisation methods on the current docs page.
flashcards.back: Supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement fine-tuning and distillation.

flashcards.front: What does reinforcement fine-tuning in Bedrock use instead of gold answers?
flashcards.back: Reward functions (for example a grader in AWS Lambda), with prompt datasets or invocation logs as input.

flashcards.front: What is model distillation?
flashcards.back: A teacher model generates responses to your prompts, and a smaller student model is fine-tuned on them to get a cheaper, faster model.

flashcards.front: What format is Bedrock fine-tuning data?
flashcards.back: JSONL: prompt/completion records, or the bedrock-conversation-2024 schema for conversational data.

flashcards.front: How do you serve a model customised in Bedrock?
flashcards.back: Purchase Provisioned Throughput (billed hourly per model unit; no commitment, 1-month or 6-month terms) or, for supported base models and Regions, create an on-demand custom model deployment.

flashcards.front: What is catastrophic forgetting?
flashcards.back: Loss of general capabilities after training on a narrow dataset. Mitigate by mixing in general data, training less aggressively and evaluating broadly.

flashcards.front: What does SageMaker Model Registry track per model version?
flashcards.back: Versions in a model package group, with metrics, lineage, Model Cards and an approval status that can trigger CI/CD deployment.

flashcards.front: What is managed MLflow on SageMaker AI used for?
flashcards.back: Experiment tracking (parameters, metrics, artifacts) through Tracking Servers or serverless MLflow Apps, with auto-registration into Model Registry.

flashcards.front: What does Bedrock Prompt Management provide?
flashcards.back: Prompts with variables, variants for comparing outputs, and immutable versions you can use at inference or in Flows.

flashcards.front: Precision and recall formulas?
flashcards.back: Precision = TP / (TP + FP). Recall = TP / (TP + FN).

flashcards.front: Why choose RMSE over MAE?
flashcards.back: RMSE squares errors before averaging, so it penalises large errors more heavily.

flashcards.front: What does ROC AUC tell you?
flashcards.back: How well a classifier ranks positives above negatives across all thresholds, independent of a chosen cut-off.

flashcards.front: ROUGE vs BLEU vs BERTScore?
flashcards.back: ROUGE: recall-oriented n-gram overlap (summaries). BLEU: precision-oriented n-gram overlap (translation). BERTScore: embedding similarity that tolerates paraphrases.

flashcards.front: What is LLM-as-a-judge in Bedrock?
flashcards.back: A judge-model evaluation where an FM scores responses on qualities such as correctness or helpfulness.

flashcards.front: How should a new AWS customer explain individual predictions now that Clarify is closed to new customers?
flashcards.back: Compute SHAP values with the open-source SHAP library.

flashcards.front: What is the status of SageMaker Debugger?
flashcards.back: In maintenance and closed to new customers from 30 Jul 2026; SageMaker Profiler is entering sunset.

flashcards.front: Which SageMaker AI inference option fits payloads up to about 1 GB and processing up to about an hour?
flashcards.back: Asynchronous inference. Requests are queued, inputs and outputs live in S3, and the endpoint can scale to zero.

flashcards.front: When should you use batch transform instead of an endpoint?
flashcards.back: When you score a whole dataset offline (for example nightly) and nobody waits for a single prediction. It leaves no persistent endpoint running.

flashcards.front: Name four things SageMaker Serverless Inference does not support.
flashcards.back: Any four of: GPUs, multi-model endpoints, VPC configuration, network isolation, data capture, multiple production variants, Model Monitor, inference pipelines.

flashcards.front: How do you reduce cold starts on a serverless endpoint, and which metric shows them?
flashcards.back: Configure Provisioned Concurrency. The OverheadLatency metric reveals cold-start overhead.

flashcards.front: Can a serverless endpoint be converted to real-time, and back?
flashcards.back: It can be converted to real-time, but a real-time endpoint cannot be converted back to serverless.

flashcards.front: What is a multi-model endpoint (MME) best for?
flashcards.back: Many similar models (same framework) invoked unevenly, such as one model per customer. Models load from S3 on demand behind one endpoint and container.

flashcards.front: What do inference components add to a SageMaker AI endpoint?
flashcards.back: Several models on one endpoint, each with its own compute allocation (accelerators, memory), scaled independently.

flashcards.front: Shadow test vs production variant split: what is the key difference?
flashcards.back: A shadow test mirrors a copy of traffic and returns only production responses. A production variant split serves real responses from each variant (A/B).

flashcards.front: Which endpoint types do not support shadow tests?
flashcards.back: Serverless, asynchronous, multi-model and multi-container endpoints (plus Marketplace containers and Inf1).

flashcards.front: What are the three traffic-shifting modes of SageMaker AI deployment guardrails?
flashcards.back: All at once, canary and linear, each with a baking period and automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarms.

flashcards.front: What must you buy to run a model you customised in Amazon Bedrock?
flashcards.back: Provisioned Throughput (billed hourly per Model Unit, no-commitment, 1-month or 6-month terms), or an on-demand custom model deployment where the base model and Region support it.

flashcards.front: What does Bedrock Custom Model Import accept, and how are imported models invoked?
flashcards.back: Hugging Face-format weights (safetensors, config, tokenizer) for supported architectures, from S3. Invoked on demand through InvokeModel.

flashcards.front: Name three things Bedrock Custom Model Import does not support.
flashcards.back: Batch inference, CloudFormation and embedding models.

flashcards.front: What does SageMaker Inference Recommender do?
flashcards.back: Load-tests candidate instance types for a model and reports latency, throughput and cost, so you can right-size before deploying.

flashcards.front: Which service scales SageMaker AI endpoints, and with what policy types?
flashcards.back: Application Auto Scaling, with target tracking, step scaling and scheduled scaling.

flashcards.front: Why might invocations per instance be a poor scaling metric for an LLM endpoint?
flashcards.back: Long generations can saturate GPUs at low request counts. Scale on a metric that reflects real load, such as GPU utilisation or concurrent requests.

flashcards.front: How does an endpoint reach resources in a private subnet?
flashcards.back: Attach a VPC configuration (private subnets, security groups) to the model, and add VPC endpoints for services such as S3. Not available on serverless.

flashcards.front: What is SageMaker HyperPod and which orchestrators does it use?
flashcards.back: Resilient clusters for FM training (and deployment) that detect and replace faulty nodes, orchestrated by Slurm or Amazon EKS.

flashcards.front: How does the AWS CDK relate to CloudFormation?
flashcards.back: The CDK defines infrastructure in code and synthesises CloudFormation templates, which CloudFormation deploys as stacks.

flashcards.front: What is AWS CodeConnections used for in ML CI/CD?
flashcards.back: Connecting CodePipeline and other AWS services to external Git providers such as GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket.

flashcards.front: How do you start a deployment automatically when a model version is approved?
flashcards.back: An EventBridge rule on the SageMaker model package state change event starts the deployment pipeline (for example CodePipeline).

flashcards.front: Which SageMaker Pipelines step gates registration on an evaluation metric?
flashcards.back: The Condition step, which branches to Register model or Fail based on a value such as accuracy.

flashcards.front: Which SageMaker Pipelines step waits for an external system to report back?
flashcards.back: The Callback step. It pauses until the external process returns success or failure.

flashcards.front: What does step caching do in SageMaker Pipelines?
flashcards.back: Reuses the result of a step whose inputs and configuration are unchanged from a previous run, saving time and cost.

flashcards.front: When is Amazon MWAA the right orchestrator?
flashcards.back: When the team already has Apache Airflow DAGs and wants a managed Airflow environment instead of rewriting workflows.

flashcards.front: Which Step Functions pattern pauses a workflow for human approval?
flashcards.back: Wait for callback with a task token. The workflow resumes when the token is returned.

flashcards.front: How do you keep a Bedrock Knowledge Base current when S3 documents change?
flashcards.back: Run an ingestion job (data source sync) on a schedule or triggered by an event, so new content is chunked, embedded and indexed.

flashcards.front: What is the status of Bedrock Agents Classic?
flashcards.back: Closed to new customers since 30 July 2026 with a frozen model catalogue. AgentCore is the recommended path.

flashcards.front: What does AgentCore Gateway do?
flashcards.back: Turns existing APIs and Lambda functions into MCP tools that agents can discover and call.

flashcards.front: MCP vs A2A?
flashcards.back: MCP connects agents to tools and data sources. A2A lets agents communicate with other agents.

flashcards.front: Which AgentCore service stores agent state across sessions?
flashcards.back: AgentCore Memory, which provides short-term (session) and long-term (cross-session) memory.

flashcards.front: Is edge deployment with SageMaker Neo on MLA-C02?
flashcards.back: No. The C02 outline removed edge model optimisation, and AWS IoT services are out of scope.

flashcards.front: What is a reranker in a RAG pipeline?
flashcards.back: A model that reorders retrieved chunks by relevance to the query before they are passed to the generator, improving answer quality.

flashcards.front: What are the four SageMaker Model Monitor monitoring types?
flashcards.back: Data quality, model quality, bias drift and feature attribution drift.

flashcards.front: Which Model Monitor type requires ground truth labels?
flashcards.back: Model quality monitoring. It merges captured predictions with actual labels to compute metrics such as accuracy or RMSE.

flashcards.front: Three ingredients of a drift monitoring setup
flashcards.back: Data capture of requests and responses, a baseline (statistics and constraints) from training data, and a scheduled comparison job that emits metrics and violations.

flashcards.front: Can new AWS customers onboard to SageMaker Model Monitor, Clarify or Debugger?
flashcards.back: No. They have been in maintenance and closed to new customers since 30 Jul 2026. Existing customers can keep using them.

flashcards.front: What does AWS recommend instead of Model Monitor for new builds?
flashcards.back: The open-source SageMaker AI monitoring solutions: MLflow Apps with Evidently AI, dashboards in Amazon Quick (QuickSight), and CloudWatch anomaly detection.

flashcards.front: Shadow test vs A/B test
flashcards.back: Shadow: copy of live traffic goes to a shadow variant, only production responses are returned. A/B: traffic is split across production variants and users receive responses from each.

flashcards.front: Endpoint types that do not support shadow tests
flashcards.back: Serverless, asynchronous, multi-model and multi-container endpoints (plus Marketplace containers and Inf1 instances).

flashcards.front: ModelLatency vs OverheadLatency
flashcards.back: ModelLatency is time inside the model container. OverheadLatency is time SageMaker adds around it; on serverless endpoints it exposes cold starts.

flashcards.front: What does CloudWatch generative AI observability show?
flashcards.back: Model invocation and AgentCore agent dashboards: invocations, input/output tokens, latency (avg, P90, P99), errors, throttling and cost attribution, with ADOT tracing.

flashcards.front: How do you capture full Bedrock prompts and responses?
flashcards.back: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging (off by default) to CloudWatch Logs and/or Amazon S3.

flashcards.front: Two agent failure modes the MLA-C02 guide asks you to monitor
flashcards.back: Truncated streaming responses and tool invocation failures.

flashcards.front: What emits OTEL traces for agents on AgentCore Runtime?
flashcards.back: AgentCore Observability, viewable in the CloudWatch agents dashboard.

flashcards.front: Tool that load-tests a model on candidate instance types
flashcards.back: SageMaker Inference Recommender. It reports latency, throughput and cost per instance type.

flashcards.front: Default target tracking metric for SageMaker endpoint auto scaling
flashcards.back: SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance.

flashcards.front: Requirement to make Managed Spot Training safe for long jobs
flashcards.back: Write checkpoints to S3 so an interrupted job resumes instead of restarting, and set a maximum wait time.

flashcards.front: When are Savings Plans the right purchasing option?
flashcards.back: For a steady, predictable baseline of compute usage over a 1- or 3-year commitment. Cover peaks with On-Demand.

flashcards.front: Budgets vs Cost Explorer vs cost allocation tags
flashcards.back: Budgets alert on thresholds; Cost Explorer analyses spend trends; tags attribute spend to projects or teams.

flashcards.front: Main FM cost levers on Bedrock
flashcards.back: Model choice, prompt caching, batch inference, capping output tokens, and Provisioned Throughput for steady volume. Customised models are served through Provisioned Throughput or, for supported base models, an on-demand custom model deployment.

flashcards.front: Can prompt caching be used with Bedrock batch inference?
flashcards.back: No. Prompt caching is not supported with batch inference.

flashcards.front: Short-term vs long-term Bedrock API keys
flashcards.back: Short-term: up to 12 hours, inherit the IAM principal's permissions, recommended for production. Long-term: create an IAM user with an expiry, for exploration only.

flashcards.front: IAM action and condition key that control Bedrock API key use
flashcards.back: bedrock:CallWithBearerToken, with the bedrock:bearerTokenType condition key.

flashcards.front: How do you keep SageMaker API and runtime traffic off the internet?
flashcards.back: Interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for the SageMaker API and runtime, plus an S3 gateway endpoint.

flashcards.front: What does SageMaker network isolation do?
flashcards.back: It blocks the training or inference container from making any outbound network calls, including to other AWS services.

flashcards.front: Which Guardrails safeguard catches RAG hallucinations?
flashcards.back: Contextual grounding checks, which score grounding against the source and relevance to the query.

flashcards.front: What is the ApplyGuardrail API for?
flashcards.back: Evaluating text against a guardrail without invoking a model, so you can screen inputs and outputs for any model, including non-Bedrock ones.

flashcards.front: Model Cards vs Model Registry vs lineage tracking
flashcards.back: Model Cards document intended use, risk and evaluation; Model Registry versions models and gates deployment by approval status; lineage links data, jobs, models and endpoints.

flashcards.front: Which services scan ML containers and code in CI/CD (Skill 4.3.1)?
flashcards.back: Amazon Inspector (container image and workload vulnerabilities) and Amazon CodeGuru (code review).

flashcards.front: CloudTrail vs AWS Config for ML governance
flashcards.back: CloudTrail records API activity (who did what). AWS Config records resource configuration history and evaluates compliance rules.

questions.stem: A data science team stores 4 TB of clickstream data in Amazon S3 as uncompressed CSV. Their Amazon Athena feature queries select 5 of 120 columns for one week at a time, and each query scans the full dataset. Which change most reduces query cost and time?
options: Compress the CSV files with gzip and keep the current layout
Convert the data to Parquet partitioned by date and update the Glue Data Catalog table
Load the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table keyed by session ID
Increase the Athena workgroup query timeout and run queries in parallel
questions.explanation: Parquet is columnar, so Athena reads only the selected columns, and date partitions let it skip weeks it does not need. Compression alone still forces full-row scans, and DynamoDB is not built for analytical scans.
rationales: Gzip lowers bytes stored but Athena must still read every column of every row.
Correct: columnar format plus partition pruning cuts the scanned data dramatically.
DynamoDB is a key-value store, not an analytics engine for column-selective scans.
More time or parallelism does not reduce the data scanned, so cost stays the same.

questions.stem: A retailer sends JSON purchase events from its web app and wants them in Amazon S3 as Parquet files for Athena and training jobs. The team wants the least operational overhead and can accept delivery delays of a few minutes. What should the ML engineer do?
options: Send events to Amazon Data Firehose with record format conversion to Parquet and an S3 destination
Send events to Amazon SQS and use a scheduled Lambda function to write CSV files
Write events to Kinesis Data Streams and run a consumer on EC2 that converts records to Parquet
Run an hourly AWS Glue crawler against the web servers' log directories
questions.explanation: Firehose is a managed delivery service that buffers records and can convert JSON to Parquet using a Glue table schema before writing to S3. A buffering delay of minutes is acceptable here, so no custom consumer is needed.
rationales: Correct: fully managed buffering, conversion and delivery.
Produces CSV, not Parquet, and adds custom batching code.
Works, but adds servers and conversion code to build and operate.
Crawlers infer schemas for the Data Catalog; they do not ingest data from web servers.

questions.stem: A payments company needs per-card features such as "number of transactions in the last 5 minutes", computed continuously from a transaction stream and available to the fraud model within seconds. Which service is best suited to compute these features?
options: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink reading from Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon Data Firehose delivering to S3, with Athena queries every 5 minutes
An AWS Glue batch ETL job scheduled every hour
AWS Glue DataBrew recipe jobs run on demand
questions.explanation: Flink provides stateful, low-latency stream processing with windowed aggregations, which fits rolling per-card counts. The other options are batch or near-batch and cannot deliver within seconds.
rationales: Correct: stateful windowed aggregation on the live stream.
Firehose buffering plus periodic queries adds minutes of delay.
Hourly batch jobs are far too slow for second-level freshness.
DataBrew is a visual batch cleaning tool, not a stream processor.

questions.stem: An ML engineer must join customer records from an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with order history files in Amazon S3, then write the merged training dataset back to S3 nightly. The team does not want to manage clusters and wants the schemas discoverable by other teams. What should the engineer use?
options: An Amazon EMR cluster with a custom bootstrap action and a cron job on the primary node
A Lambda function that queries RDS and reads all S3 files in memory
AWS Glue crawlers to catalog both sources and a scheduled AWS Glue ETL job to join them
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to replicate RDS rows into S3
questions.explanation: Glue is serverless Spark ETL with crawlers and a Data Catalog, so it joins JDBC and S3 sources without clusters and publishes schemas for reuse. EMR would work but requires managing clusters, which the team wants to avoid.
rationales: Meets the join need but means managing a cluster and scheduler.
Lambda memory and runtime limits make this fragile for large datasets.
Correct: serverless join plus shared catalog schemas.
Kinesis is for streaming events, not nightly batch joins.

questions.stem: A company is migrating large on-premises Spark jobs that depend on custom native libraries and specific Spark configuration tuning. Jobs run for several hours on hundreds of nodes, and engineers need control over instance types and installed software. Which AWS service best fits?
options: AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon EMR
AWS Lambda with Step Functions fan-out
Amazon Athena with CREATE TABLE AS SELECT
questions.explanation: Amazon EMR runs managed Spark clusters where you choose instance types, install custom software and tune configuration. That control is what these long-running, library-heavy jobs need.
rationales: DataBrew is a visual tool and cannot run custom Spark code.
Correct: managed clusters with full control over software and configuration.
Lambda time and memory limits do not suit multi-hour distributed Spark jobs.
Athena runs SQL and cannot host custom native Spark libraries.

questions.stem: A team is choosing a storage format for wide analytical tables whose queries read only a few columns at a time. Which formats are columnar and best fit this access pattern? (Select two.)
options: Apache Parquet
CSV
Apache ORC
JSON Lines
Apache Avro
questions.explanation: Parquet and ORC store data by column with compression, so engines read only the needed columns. CSV and JSON Lines are row-oriented text and must be read in full.
rationales: Correct: columnar and compressed.
Row-oriented text; every column is read.
Correct: columnar and compressed.
Row-oriented and verbose; suited to semi-structured records, not column scans.
Avro is a row-oriented binary format suited to record serialisation, not column-selective scans.

questions.stem: A legal firm wants a Bedrock Knowledge Base over 20 million archived documents. Lawyers query it a few times a day, and the main requirement is the lowest storage cost with sub-second query latency. Embeddings are standard float vectors. Which vector store should the ML engineer choose?
options: Amazon S3 Vectors
An OpenSearch Service managed cluster sized for peak traffic
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector on provisioned instances
Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with a custom index
questions.explanation: S3 Vectors is documented as cost-effective with sub-second queries and best suited to infrequent query workloads, which matches a large archive queried a few times a day. Always-on clusters cost more for low query volume.
rationales: Correct: low-cost storage for infrequent, sub-second queries on float vectors.
Supported, but running a cluster for a few daily queries is not the lowest-cost option.
Supported, but provisioned database instances cost more for this access pattern.
ElastiCache is not a supported Knowledge Base vector store.

questions.stem: To shrink index size, an ML engineer wants a Bedrock Knowledge Base to store binary vector embeddings. Which vector store supports this?
options: Amazon S3 Vectors
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector
Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
Amazon Neptune Analytics
questions.explanation: For Knowledge Bases, only OpenSearch Serverless and OpenSearch Service managed clusters support binary vectors. S3 Vectors accepts float embeddings only.
rationales: S3 Vectors supports float embeddings only.
Not listed as supporting binary vectors for Knowledge Bases.
Correct: OpenSearch is the only family that supports binary vectors here.
Neptune Analytics is used for GraphRAG, not binary vectors.

questions.stem: Security requires all vector data to stay off the public internet. An engineer creates an OpenSearch Service managed domain with VPC-only access and tries to use it as the vector store for a Bedrock Knowledge Base, but setup fails. What is the best next step?
options: Add a NAT gateway to the domain's subnets
Use an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection or another supported store instead of the VPC-only domain
